rfp_analysis.detected_priority_note: The RFP rules out a database migration and asks for rollout with minimal disruption. Proposals that change NordFrame’s infrastructure should lose points.

requirements.text: A web-based dashboard showing real-time inventory levels across all 6 warehouses.
Alerts to warehouse managers when items fall below a configurable threshold.
Integration with the existing PostgreSQL inventory database, with no migration to a new database.
requirements.source_quote: no migration to a new database

requirements.text: Warehouse managers see only their own site; HQ staff see all sites.
A data migration / onboarding plan for all 6 sites with minimal disruption.
Support and maintenance terms after go-live, including response times and SLAs.
Clear documentation of assumptions, limitations or risks, since inventory decisions will rely on the system.
€80,000–€120,000 total, including the first year of support.
requirements.source_quote: €80,000–€120,000 total, including first year of support

requirements.text: Working pilot at one warehouse within 3 months; all 6 sites within 6 months.
requirements.source_quote: Working pilot at one warehouse within 3 months

suggested_criteria_weights.name: Completeness vs RFP Requirements
suggested_criteria_weights.description: Every explicit RFP requirement is addressed.
suggested_criteria_weights.priority_reason: The RFP lists seven numbered requirements and puts each one in bold. A buyer who writes a checklist reads the answer as a checklist.

suggested_criteria_weights.name: Risk/Assumptions Transparency
suggested_criteria_weights.description: Dependencies and risks are flagged, not hidden.
suggested_criteria_weights.priority_reason: Requirement 7 explains why it is asked for, which is rare. The client is telling you that hidden risk is the thing they fear.

source_refs.quote: inventory decisions will be made based on this system

suggested_criteria_weights.name: Pricing Clarity
suggested_criteria_weights.description: Price stated, broken down, easy to follow.
suggested_criteria_weights.priority_reason: The budget is published as a range and states that it includes the first year of support, so a vague price is easy to spot.

source_refs.quote: €80,000–€120,000 total, including first year of support

suggested_criteria_weights.name: Timeline Clarity
suggested_criteria_weights.priority_reason: Two hard dates are given: a pilot at one site within 3 months and all 6 sites within 6 months.

source_refs.quote: Working pilot at one warehouse within 3 months

suggested_criteria_weights.name: Data Accuracy & Validation
suggested_criteria_weights.description: Says how inventory figures are checked against reality before anyone relies on them.
suggested_criteria_weights.priority_reason: The RFP does not list this as a requirement, but it gives the reason behind Requirement 7: stock decisions will be made from this dashboard. A proposal that never says how the numbers are verified leaves that risk with the client.

source_refs.quote: inventory decisions will be made based on this system

suggested_criteria_weights.name: Problem Understanding
suggested_criteria_weights.description: Reflects the client’s actual stated problem and goals, not a generic pitch.
suggested_criteria_weights.priority_reason: Worth checking, but Completeness already tests it against each requirement. Scoring both at a high weight counts the same gap twice.

source_refs.quote: 6 regional warehouses across Germany and Austria

suggested_criteria_weights.name: Scope & Deliverables Clarity
suggested_criteria_weights.description: Deliverables are specific; clear what is and isn’t included.
suggested_criteria_weights.priority_reason: Same overlap as Problem understanding: the scope constraints sit inside the numbered requirements.

source_refs.quote: no migration to a new database

suggested_criteria_weights.name: Tone & Persuasiveness
suggested_criteria_weights.description: Reads as confident, client-focused and professional, not boilerplate.
suggested_criteria_weights.priority_reason: The RFP says nothing about presentation, and this buyer is working through a checklist. Worth fixing, but it rarely decides a deal on its own.

suggested_criteria_weights.name: Legacy System & Spreadsheets
suggested_criteria_weights.description: Says what happens to the old legacy system and the spreadsheets after go-live.
suggested_criteria_weights.priority_reason: The legacy system appears only in the Background, never in the numbered requirements, so the checklist will not catch a proposal that ignores it. Someone still has to switch it off.

source_refs.quote: split across spreadsheets and an outdated legacy system

scoring.verdict: Every RFP requirement is addressed with specifics. Two small clarifications, on out-of-hours support and cost after Year 1, would remove the remaining ambiguity.

criteria.name: Completeness vs RFP Requirements
criteria.comment: All 7 requirements, budget and timeline addressed.

criteria.name: Risk/Assumptions Transparency
criteria.comment: Three concrete assumptions, each with its effect on the schedule.

criteria.name: Pricing Clarity
criteria.comment: Itemised €102,000 total inside the budget, with Year 1 support as its own line.

criteria.name: Timeline Clarity
criteria.comment: Week-based plan mapped to both targets: pilot in Weeks 1–10, rollout in Weeks 13–24.

criteria.name: Data Accuracy & Validation
criteria.comment: A 2-week parallel run against the existing spreadsheet process before cutover, stated as the way data accuracy is confirmed.
citations: running in parallel with existing spreadsheet process

criteria.name: Problem Understanding
criteria.comment: Reflects the 6 sites in Germany and Austria and the client’s goal of not disrupting existing infrastructure.

criteria.name: Scope & Deliverables Clarity
criteria.comment: Each requirement has its own section with concrete behaviour, such as access enforced at database query level.
citations: enforced at the database query level

criteria.name: Tone & Persuasiveness
criteria.comment: Confident and specific throughout. The references are credible but unnamed.

criteria.name: Legacy System & Spreadsheets
criteria.comment: The spreadsheets keep running during validation, which covers the transition. Switching off the legacy system is still not addressed.
citations: running in parallel with existing spreadsheet process

findings.reason: Live levels across all 6 warehouses, continuously refreshed.
findings.citation: Live inventory levels across all 6 warehouses

findings.reason: Per-item thresholds; email or SMS to the responsible manager.
Read-only connector to the existing database; no migration or schema changes.
Site-level access, enforced in the database queries rather than hidden in the UI.
findings.citation: enforced at the database query level

findings.reason: Pilot, a 2-week parallel run against the spreadsheets, then 2 rollout batches.
findings.citation: running in parallel with existing spreadsheet process

findings.reason: Critical support only covers business hours. A “system down” issue gets a 24-hour response but only “during CET business hours”, so an outage on Friday evening could wait until Monday.
findings.suggested_patch: State cover for critical incidents outside business hours, for example: “Critical issues (system down) are handled 24/7 with a 4-hour response; minor issues within 3 business days during CET business hours.”

findings.reason: Database access, site contacts and threshold tuning, each with its impact.
Cost after Year 1 isn’t stated. The client will need to budget for support from Year 2.
findings.suggested_patch: Add a line: “Support & maintenance from Year 2: €18,000 per year on the same terms.”

findings.reason: Pilot in Weeks 1–10 and rollout in Weeks 13–24, each mapped to the client’s target.
